content.title: About
content.content: Beignet is a traditional French fried dough pastry, often dusted with powdered sugar. The batter is usually made from flour, eggs, milk, butter and yeast, then small portions are deep‑fried until golden. The taste is mildly sweet with a crisp outer crust and a soft, airy interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beignets are especially popular in New Orleans, where they are commonly served with powdered sugar and coffee.
The classic recipe uses a yeasted dough, but there are quick‑rise versions that rely on baking powder.
In France, beignets are sold as round “pancake‑like” treats from street stalls.
They became famous in the U.S. through the Café du Monde brand in the late 19th century.
Both sweet and savory versions exist; savory beignets may contain cheese, ham or seafood.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Beignets provide carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Eggs and milk in the batter add a modest amount of animal protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeasted dough is a source of B1, B2 and B6 vitamins, important for metabolism.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Flour and yeast contribute a small amount of iron, supporting blood health.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Milk and butter add calcium, beneficial for bone strength.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Because they are deep‑fried, beignets are high in calories and saturated fats.

items.title: Sugar
items.content: They are often dusted with powdered sugar, increasing simple sugar intake.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The batter is typically made with wheat flour, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Trans fats from reused oil
items.content: Reusing frying oil can create trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve beignets hot, dusted with powdered sugar, with honey, fruit sauce, or plain. They can be split and filled with sweet cream, jam, or savory fillings such as cheese and ham.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Beignets are best enjoyed fresh and hot. If needed, keep them in an airtight container at room temperature for 1‑2 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a bag and reheat in the oven before serving.
